res.mechanism:
Theme templates, the same way robots.txt.liquid works. Shopify documents three Liquid-only templates (they cannot be JSON) in the theme's templates/ folder: templates/agents.md.liquid, templates/llms.txt.liquid and templates/llms-full.txt.liquid. You can add them in Admin > Online Store > Themes > ... > Edit code > Add a new template (options: agents.md, llms.txt, llms-full.txt). Pushing them with the CLI should also work, but that is inferred and not tested here.

Which template serves each URL (first one found wins):
- /agents.md: agents.md.liquid, then the Shopify default
- /llms.txt: llms.txt.liquid, then agents.md.liquid, then the Shopify default
- /llms-full.txt: llms-full.txt.liquid, then agents.md.liquid, then the Shopify default

Adding only templates/llms.txt.liquid replaces /llms.txt and nothing else. The template accepts plain text or Markdown plus Liquid. The Liquid context is restricted to two objects:
- `request`
- `agents`, with 7 properties: store_name, store_url ("using the bare primary domain"), ucp_discovery_url, mcp_endpoint_url, ucp_versions, currency, sitemap_url

shop, collections, pages, linklists, articles and blogs are not available and render blank. No documented object exposes the Shopify default text (nothing like robots.default_groups), so a custom file fully replaces the default. To keep the UCP, policy or Shop-skill sections you must rebuild them from agents.* or hardcode them.

No admin setting controls these files: the Agentic storefronts settings pages cover only Catalog access, direct checkout and auto-enroll. The DWF file (seo/llms-txt/dwf-llms.txt) contains no {{ or {% delimiters, so it can be pasted as-is.

Checked in the repo: templates/ currently holds robots.txt.liquid and no agents or llms template, which matches the live file being Shopify's default. Live response headers show theme;desc="158031413515" and pageType "llms_txt", so the request goes through the live theme.
res.applies_per_domain_or_market:
Partly documented, partly inferred.

Documented:
- All three templates render with the `request` object available. `request` has host, origin and locale.
- The docs say each file "is served at the bare primary domain, without a locale or Shopify Markets subfolder prefix. It has no localized counterpart."
- agents.store_url uses the bare primary domain.
- Shopify shows request.host branching for robots.txt.liquid (dev doc and merchant changelog of 25 Mar 2025). It gives no such example for the agents or llms templates, and the docs do not cover separate ccTLD market domains.

Observed on this store (one request per domain, 14 Sep 2026):
- www.alessandrodesign.hu/llms.txt returns 200 with Content-Language hu-HU and a different ETag hash from .ro.
- Its content is identical to .ro except that the four policy titles are in Hungarian.
- Every URL in it still points to https://www.alessandrodesign.ro. So Shopify serves the same file on all market domains, varying only the policy titles by locale, and all links go to the primary domain.

Inferred: a custom template will be served on every market domain, since all domains use the same live theme. Per-domain content should be possible with {% if request.host == 'www.alessandrodesign.hu' %} or {{ request.origin }}. Otherwise the DWF Romanian file would appear verbatim on .hu, .fr, .eu and the other domains. This is not verified. Test on an unpublished theme before relying on it, and check that caching varies by host (the differing ETags suggest it does).
res.agents_md_and_llms_full:
It depends on which template is added:
- templates/llms.txt.liquid changes /llms.txt only. /agents.md and /llms-full.txt keep the Shopify default. The docs say so directly: the template "takes precedence for /llms.txt only, while /agents.md and /llms-full.txt are unaffected".
- templates/agents.md.liquid changes all three URLs, unless a dedicated llms template overrides one of them.
- templates/llms-full.txt.liquid changes /llms-full.txt only.

The Help Center says the same: if agents.md.liquid and a URL-specific template both exist, the URL-specific one defines that URL.

Today (observed): /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt carry the default content and differ only in the line naming which file you are reading. Their text states that /agents.md is canonical and that the file mirrors it.

For the DWF request, the least invasive option is to add only templates/llms.txt.liquid. /agents.md and /llms-full.txt would keep Shopify's managed UCP/agent file, which Shopify recommends keeping.
res.redirects_or_other_workarounds:
URL redirects (Admin > Content > Menus > View URL redirects; older docs say Online Store > Navigation) will not work for /llms.txt. The Help Center says redirects work only from broken URLs: if a URL still loads a valid page, the redirect won't work, and redirects only work for URLs that return 404. /llms.txt always returns 200 because Shopify serves a default whenever no template exists, so it can never qualify.

A community report on the Shopify dev forum (Nordalux, 11 May 2026) confirms this in practice: an existing /llms.txt redirect stopped being honored once Shopify began serving the file natively. Nothing in the docs mentions /llms.txt specifically; this is the general rule applied to it.

App-proxy workarounds were also reported overridden (Lynn_lin, 21 May 2026). A Cloudflare or other proxy in front of Shopify is discouraged by the Help Center, which says Shopify doesn't recommend one and can't support it. The only supported way to change the file is the theme templates above.
res.robots_txt_notes:
What Shopify documents:
- The "Customize robots.txt" dev doc says rules that aren't part of a default group can be entered manually outside the Liquid that outputs the defaults.
- Its examples are User-agent/Disallow/Allow blocks and an extra `Sitemap: [sitemap-url]` line.
- The robots-txt-liquid page and the Help Center both say the whole template can be replaced with plain text rules, which they strongly advise against.
- The Help Center lists the supported edits: allow or disallow URLs, crawl-delay rules, extra sitemap URLs, blocking crawlers. It also says robots.txt.liquid edits are unsupported by Shopify Support.
- robots.txt.liquid can use request.host (changelog 25 Mar 2025, plus the dev doc), so lines can differ per market domain.

What Shopify does not document: comment lines (#) or arbitrary non-directive lines. Neither is mentioned in any Shopify doc found.

Inference: the template is plain Liquid, so literal text outside tags is output as written. A "# LLMs.txt" comment should pass through unchanged.

Google's robots.txt doc (last updated 2026-08-31) says everything after # is ignored and invalid lines are ignored. The DWF line "https://www.alessandrodesign.ro/llms.txt" is therefore a comment-less, invalid line with no effect for Google. If a pointer is wanted, it is safer to put it in a comment, e.g. "# LLMs.txt: https://www.alessandrodesign.ro/llms.txt".

Caveats:
- The Help Center notes that uploading a theme ZIP from the Themes page won't import robots.txt.liquid, while ThemeKit/CLI keeps it. Whether that also applies to agents.md.liquid or llms.txt.liquid is not documented.
- The existing template is CRLF, and the live output uses lone-CR line breaks; keep this in mind when adding lines.

res.summary:
Yes. Shopify documents a supported override that works like robots.txt.liquid.

1) When and why. The official docs and changelogs never announce when auto-serving started. The only official post is the dev changelog "Customize /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt and /agents.md" (posted 28 May 2026, effective 29 May 2026, updated 4 Jun 2026). The Shopify dev forum shows the routes already live by 8 May 2026. Shopify places the files under its agentic storefronts / Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) agent-discovery work:
- /agents.md is the canonical agent-facing description: UCP discovery at /.well-known/ucp, the MCP endpoint, browsing URLs, policies and the Shop skill.
- /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt are alternate URLs kept for older AI crawlers, mirroring /agents.md.
- A Shopify staff member on the forum (20 May 2026) said /agents.md is now the primary storefront discovery file for agentic and AI experiences.
- Related releases: the Agentic Storefronts admin page (11 May 2026) and Storefront Catalog MCP implementing UCP (22 Apr 2026).

2) Customization. Add templates/llms.txt.liquid, templates/llms-full.txt.liquid and/or templates/agents.md.liquid (Liquid only; addable in Edit code via Add a new template).
- Order for /llms.txt: llms.txt.liquid, then agents.md.liquid, then the Shopify default.
- The templates see only `request` and a 7-property `agents` object; `shop`, `collections` and similar render blank.
- No object exposes the default text, and there is no admin setting. A custom file fully replaces the default.

3) Scope.
- llms.txt.liquid affects only /llms.txt.
- agents.md.liquid affects all three URLs unless a dedicated template overrides one.
- The docs say the files live at the bare primary domain with no localized counterpart, and agents.store_url is the primary domain.
- On this store, www.alessandrodesign.hu/llms.txt already returns the default with Hungarian policy titles but .ro URLs (one request, 14 Sep 2026).
- A single template will be served on every market domain. Per-domain variants should be possible through request.host or request.origin, which are available, but Shopify gives no example for these templates. This needs a test.

4) URL redirects. The Help Center says redirects work only from broken (404) URLs. /llms.txt always returns 200, so a redirect can't take effect. Forum users confirmed existing /llms.txt redirects stopped being honored.

5) robots.txt. Shopify docs allow manual plain-text rules outside the default Liquid loop, per-domain lines via request.host, or a full plain-text replacement (discouraged). They never mention # comments or arbitrary lines. Liquid passes literal text through, so a "# LLMs.txt" comment should appear in the output. Google ignores comments and invalid lines, so DWF's bare-URL line would do nothing for Google; it is better written as a comment.

res.mechanism:
Shopify documents and supports this: add a Liquid template named `templates/llms.txt.liquid` to the theme. It cannot be a JSON template. Shopify serves it at /llms.txt with Content-Type text/markdown, in place of the auto-generated file. The lookup order for /llms.txt is: llms.txt.liquid, then agents.md.liquid, then the Shopify-generated default. The feature appeared quietly in early May 2026 and was announced in the shopify.dev changelog on 28 May 2026. For our repo that means one new file, templates/llms.txt.liquid, containing the DWF text, added to live theme 158031413515. This repo already deploys templates/robots.txt.liquid through the CLI, and CLI 4.8.0 pushes anything matching `templates/**/*.{liquid,json}`, so the new file should deploy the same way (I did not push anything).

Things to know before doing it:
(a) The template only gets the `request` and `agents` objects. `shop`, `collections`, `pages` and similar render blank, so the content has to be hard-coded. That is fine here: the DWF file is plain UTF-8 with LF line endings and no `{` or `}` characters, so it can be pasted as-is (wrapping it in `{% raw %}` is optional).
(b) The theme is shared by every market domain. As observed today, the same file is served on www.alessandrodesign.eu and www.alessandrodesign.hu, so a plain template would also serve the Romanian DWF text on .eu, .hu, .fr and the rest. You can branch on `request.host`, which the docs list as available. I have not tested that inside this template.
(c) The docs say the file lives only at the bare root, with no /ro/ or /en/ version. Today /ro/llms.txt and /en/llms.txt return 404.
(d) /agents.md and /llms-full.txt stay on Shopify's default unless you also add agents.md.liquid or llms-full.txt.liquid.
(e) The file lives in the theme, so it disappears if the store switches to another theme.
(f) A 256 KB theme-file limit is mentioned only by forum users. The DWF file is 13 KB.
(g) Use LF line endings. The existing robots.txt.liquid has CRLF endings and that leaks stray CR characters into the live robots.txt.

Uploading a file to the root is not possible. A Shopify URL redirect for /llms.txt is no longer honoured because the route now returns 200. App proxies can only live under /a, /apps, /community or /tools.

A second, unofficial route exists only for .ro: alessandrodesign.ro sits on a Cloudflare zone the merchant controls (nameservers cartman/elisabeth.ns.cloudflare.com). Both www and the bare domain are proxied through Cloudflare (A records 104.26.10.139, 104.26.11.139 and 172.67.74.11, which belong to Cloudflare, not Shopify's 23.227.38.x). That is Cloudflare's O2O setup, where the merchant's Cloudflare zone handles requests before Shopify does. So a Cloudflare Worker or Snippet on /llms.txt would run first; a Shopify store with the same DNS pattern still serves a Worker-made llms.txt today. The theme template is simpler and officially supported.

Lookup order: llms.txt.liquid, then agents.md.liquid, then the generated default. The template must be Liquid, not JSON. res.summary:
Yes. You can replace Shopify's auto-generated /llms.txt with a theme template, and Shopify documents this.

**How it works**
- Add `templates/llms.txt.liquid` to the theme. Lookup order for /llms.txt: llms.txt.liquid, then agents.md.liquid, then Shopify's default.
- Timeline:
  - Shopify quietly started serving /llms.txt around 7–14 May 2026. Admin URL redirects and app-proxy setups for that path stopped working.
  - For about a week (20–27 May) /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt redirected to /agents.md.
  - Per-path templates were honoured again from 27 May and announced in the shopify.dev changelog on 28 May 2026.
- Forum posts confirm it works (Nordalux, 11 May: "Tested on our store – works as expected"). Today I checked three stores serving custom files rendered by their theme: spiritualgangster.com, vrggrl.com and basic-maintenance.com. The last one used an app proxy before and now uses a theme template.

**Apps**
- The app listings mostly don't say how they publish. The ones that do use a redirect from /llms.txt to a file they host or proxy.
- App proxies can only live under /a, /apps, /community or /tools, so an app can't serve the root path.
- To write the template into your theme, an app needs a write_themes exemption from Shopify.

**Reference themes**

skeptics.reasoning:
I looked for ways the plan could fail on this store: gating, templates being ignored, /agents.md breaking, preview, caching, per-market behaviour and robots.txt comments. None of these broke the core conclusion. Adding templates/llms.txt.liquid is documented, other stores use it today, and it changes /llms.txt only. The findings below correct small details or close questions the three reports left open.

1) Templates are honoured today, and /agents.md survives. A forum post (lumine, community.shopify.com thread 679943 #2, 11 Sep 2026) says stores with a hand-written llms.txt return 404 on /agents.md. That does not hold for theme-template stores. I made one GET each to three stores whose /llms.txt is rendered by their theme: spiritualgangster.com, www.vrggrl.com and basic-maintenance.com. On all three, /agents.md returned 200 with Shopify's default text (pageType agents_md, AgentsMdController). On the first two, /llms-full.txt also returned the default (pageType llms_full_txt). So llms.txt.liquid leaves the other two URLs alone, as the docs say.

2) The content type question is settled. All three custom-template responses are Content-Type text/markdown; charset=utf-8, the same as the default (saved in work/r2-community/http/ext-*.headers.txt).

3) The template can be tested on an unpublished theme first. This was an open question in the reports. On .ro, /llms.txt?preview_theme_id=181808693515 returns a 302 that sets the preview cookie. With that cookie, the next /llms.txt request is 200 text/markdown with server-timing theme 181808693515 and pageType llms_txt. The same happens on www.alessandrodesign.eu (content-language en-BE). A template pushed to that unpublished theme could therefore be checked on each market domain, including whether request.host branching works, before the live theme is touched. The body is still Shopify's default because that theme has no template.

4) One inference in the reports is unsound. They read the different ETag hashes on .ro and .hu as a sign that caching varies by host. The hash is not a content hash:
- the identical .ro body had ETag 0b5f7fd7… at 09:20 and 0a38a907… at 09:28;
- the identical .hu body had 09f14f76… at 09:29 and b66cc1b6… at 09:35;
- the preview render of the identical .ro body got a third hash.
The real evidence that rendering varies by domain is the text itself: policy titles are Hungarian on .hu and English on .eu. Every market domain here has its own language, so request.host branching would probably survive a cache keyed by locale. That is still an inference until tested via preview.

5) robots.txt comments pass through. Two observations support this:
- Shopify's own robots.txt output contains a # line (spiritualgangster.com/robots.txt line 2: "# we use Shopify as our ecommerc platform").
- This store's template output copies literal text exactly, including the "\r\n    " before "Disallow: /*?filter.v.*".
A fresh GET of live robots.txt found 166 lone CRs, 1 CRLF and 1 LF. The CRs come from whitespace-control tags in the CRLF template, which strip the spaces and \n but leave the \r. A parser that splits lines only on LF already sees the file as roughly one line. For such a parser, a "# LLMs.txt" line inserted before the lone LF would also turn the rest of that line into a comment. Google splits on CR, so Google is unaffected. Fix the line endings (LF template, no stray \r) before adding lines. DWF's bare URL line contains a colon, so Google reads it as an unknown "https" field and ignores it. Putting the URL inside a comment remains the cleaner option.

6) Gaps none of the reports raised:
- The DWF file includes contact@alessandrodesign.ro and two phone numbers. The agents-md-liquid doc says to avoid "contact email addresses or phone numbers" because the file is broadly cached and served to every agent. The details are public business contacts, so this is not a blocker, but it goes against Shopify's guidance.
- The live theme dawn/aless is connected to GitHub through Shopify's integration. shopify[bot] commits "Update from Shopify for theme dawn/aless" to branch aless of Kanghu/dawn; the last was 3c3bc6c6 on 11 Sep 2026. robots.txt.liquid itself entered the repo that way (f46395ca, 20 Jul 2026). Inference: a new llms.txt.liquid added through admin or CLI would also be committed back to aless, and the deploy flow should account for that.
- Shopify has already changed this behaviour once without notice. Between 20 and 27 May 2026, llms templates were ignored and /llms.txt redirected to /agents.md. At the time, Shopify staff (Liam-Shopify, 20 May) said /llms.txt "is no longer the right place to customize". The current docs still advise adding llms.txt.liquid only for "an advanced requirement". The override works today but could regress, so monitor it after deployment.

7) Still unverified:
- whether request.host is populated inside llms.txt.liquid (now testable via preview);
- whether the merchant's Cloudflare zone on .ro blocks AI-crawler user agents. I did not test this, because the rules require a browser User-Agent. Live robots.txt shows no Cloudflare-managed AI block, and nothing in it disallows /llms.txt for the * group.

Net result: the combined conclusion is not wrong or materially incomplete. The refinements above tighten it.
skeptics.corrected_conclusion:
The conclusion holds, with refinements.

- **Mechanism.** Add templates/llms.txt.liquid to the live theme 158031413515 containing the DWF text. This is documented, and other stores use it today. /llms.txt then serves that file as text/markdown. /agents.md and /llms-full.txt keep Shopify's default; this was confirmed on three stores with custom templates, which contradicts the forum claim that /agents.md turns into a 404.
- **Test first on an unpublished theme.** preview_theme_id works on the /llms.txt route on .ro and .eu (server-timing shows theme 181808693515). Push the template to 181808693515, then check /llms.txt with the preview cookie on each market domain. That also answers the one real unknown: whether `{% if request.host == ... %}` works. Without branching, the Romanian DWF file would appear on .hu, .eu, .fr and every other domain.
- **Caching evidence.** The ETag hash is not a content hash, so it says nothing about per-host caching. The evidence that rendering varies by domain is the localized policy titles on .hu and .eu.
- **Other workarounds.** URL redirects and app proxies can't serve /llms.txt. A Cloudflare Worker would work for .ro only and isn't supported by Shopify.
- **robots.txt.**
  - Literal text in robots.txt.liquid, including # lines, is output as written.
  - The live file is separated by lone CRs (166 of them) because the CRLF template uses whitespace-control tags. Convert the template to LF first.

result.summary:
I reviewed seo/llms-txt/dwf-llms.txt (259 lines, 103 link lines, 79 unique URLs) against the llms.txt proposal, the live .ro navigation and Shopify's own /llms.txt. Everything was checked live on 2026-09-14, about 09:20-09:40 UTC. Requests went out one at a time with 0.8-1 s gaps, with no 429s. Nothing was pushed or changed.

MAIN FINDING (seen directly, not inferred): 33 of the 79 unique URLs do not resolve as intended, which is 37 of the 103 link lines.
- 29 return HTTP 404.
- 4 return a 301 redirect. One of them sends the "Lustre" link to the wrong category: /collections/lustre (L47) redirects to /collections/candelabre.
- The DWF handles look like tidied-up names rather than the real handles, e.g. aplice-interior instead of aplice-de-interior, iluminat-exterior instead of iluminat-de-exterior, calorifer-electric instead of calorifel-electric.
- The live menu has a working handle for every broken collection link. All 28 of those handles return products (counted via products.json). The full per-line mapping is in seo/llms-txt/work/v3-spec/dwf-url-audit.tsv.
- The 4 broken /pages/ and /policies/ links: 2 have working pages in the footer (/pages/dropshipment, /pages/comenzi-engross). The other 2 have no page of their own: /pages/colaborari (only the already-listed colaborari-marketing exists) and /policies/cookie-policy (the footer's cookie link points to /policies/privacy-policy).
- /blogs/idei-de-amenajare (L146, L256) is 404; the real page is /pages/idei-de-amenajare.

Structure: the H1 and the blockquote are correct. After that the file breaks the format in several ways:
- There is prose inside the link sections (18 lines in 15 of the 18 H2 sections).
- 4 H2 sections contain no links at all.
- 47 list items are not links.
- There are 6 H3 headings, which the format does not define.
- None of the 103 links has a ":" description.
- There is no "## Optional" section.
Rebuilding the parser from the reference implementation (AnswerDotAI llms_txt, using its regexes) shows it would fail on 65 lines and read the H3s as sections named "# Lustre" etc.

Duplicates: 16 URLs appear more than once (40 occurrences, 24 of them redundant). Four whole sections contain only links repeated from elsewhere: "Despre" (5/5), "Categorii principale" (8/8), "Catalog" (1/1) and "Pagini importante" (11/11).

Encoding is clean: valid UTF-8, no BOM, LF line endings, no trailing whitespace. The Romanian letters are consistently the correct comma-below forms: ș U+0219 ×40 and ț U+021B ×61, with no cedilla forms. The only flaw is a missing newline at the end of the file.

Replacing Shopify's auto-generated file with this one would lose:
- the UCP discovery and MCP endpoints
- the checkout/human-approval and rate-limit rules
- the read-only JSON endpoints
- the refund-policy link
- the /agents.md pointer
/agents.md itself stays online (200, identical content). A merged file is advisable. A draft that passes the format check and uses only live-verified URLs is at seo/llms-txt/work/v3-spec/draft-merged-llms.ro.txt (94 unique links, no duplicates, 0 parser failures). The 9 blog links in it were taken from the live blog listing but not fetched one by one, and sitemap.xml was not fetched.

result.encoding_and_format: Python byte scan of seo/llms-txt/dwf-llms.txt as saved (the original delivery bytes were not available): 13,171 bytes. Strict UTF-8 decode OK. No BOM (the first bytes are '# Al'; a BOM is optional in the spec anyway). Line endings are LF only: 258 LF, 0 CRLF, 0 lone CR. No newline at end of file: the last bytes are '.ro/)', so L259 is unterminated, a minor issue that some tools warn about. No trailing spaces or tabs on any line, no tab characters, no double blank lines. The text is NFC-normalized, with no combining marks (U+0326/U+0327 = 0) and no NBSP or zero-width characters. Romanian diacritics are consistent and correct: ș U+0219 LATIN SMALL LETTER S WITH COMMA BELOW ×40, ț U+021B T WITH COMMA BELOW ×61, ă U+0103 ×53, â U+00E2 ×9, î U+00EE ×9, Î U+00CE ×1. Zero cedilla forms (ş U+015F / ţ U+0163 / Ş / Ţ = 0) and no capital Ș/Ț. Comma-below letters appear on 48 lines, with no mixing. The only other non-ASCII character is the EN DASH U+2013 ×2, both on L238 ('Luni–Vineri, 10:00–18:00'). All URLs are ASCII. Style note (not an error): the live site's menu labels, page titles and meta descriptions follow a no-diacritics house style ('Decoratiuni Perete', 'Politica de confidentialitate'), while this file uses full diacritics. That is fine and arguably better for LLMs, but anchors will not match on-page text exactly. For comparison, Shopify's live /llms.txt is also UTF-8, no BOM, LF, and ends with a newline; its only diacritic is ț U+021B ×1 (plus 10 em dashes). It is served as 'Content-Type: text/markdown; charset=utf-8'. Any replacement should keep charset=utf-8 explicitly, or Romanian letters may be mis-decoded.

What I saw, 2026-09-14:
(a) The .ro homepage lists alternate-language versions (hreflang) for 11 domains: ro and x-default=.ro, en-BE/CH/DE/ES/IE/NL/PT=.eu, cs-CZ=.cz, fr-FR=.fr, it-IT=.it, ro-IT=.it/ro, pl-PL=.pl, bg-BG=.bg, ro-HR=.hr (Romanian content on .hr), el-GR=.gr, hu-HU=.hu, sk-SK=.sk.
(b) Shopify serves /llms.txt on each domain separately. One request each: .hu gives 200 text/markdown, content-language hu-HU, its own ETag; .eu gives 200, content-language en-BE. The body is identical to .ro except the policy labels, which are machine-translated (hu 'Közlekedés' for the shipping policy, en 'Transportation'). Every absolute URL still points to www.alessandrodesign.ro (L3 store URL, L27-28 UCP endpoints, L70-73 policy links), so even the default file sends Hungarian or English agents to the Romanian domain.
(c) Collection handles are translated per market: https://www.alessandrodesign.hu/collections/oglinzi-led returns 301 to /collections/led-tukrok.

Recommendations:
1) The DWF/merged Romanian file belongs on www.alessandrodesign.ro only. It says 'magazin online din România', links .ro URLs (RON prices, Romanian pages) and has Romanian-only phone and hours. Served on .hu/.pl/.bg/.gr/.cz/.sk/.fr/.it/.eu it would contradict those domains' hreflang and send agents across markets.
2) Whatever mechanism is chosen must switch content by host. A single host-agnostic override would put the RO file on all 11 domains, because they share one theme and one Shopify storefront. The same applies to the requested robots.txt lines: templates/robots.txt.liquid is shared, so a hard-coded 'https://www.alessandrodesign.ro/llms.txt' would appear in every market's robots.txt. Also, a bare URL line is not a robots.txt directive (RFC 9309 only defines user-agent/allow/disallow plus sitemap as a common extension), and llmstxt.org does not ask for a robots.txt entry, so crawlers will ignore it.
3) Short term, leave Shopify's auto-generated file on the non-RO domains. It is accurate about UCP, and UCP handles market pricing through context.address_country and context.currency. The .ro-absolute policy links are a Shopify-side limitation.
4) Medium term, if per-host serving is possible, write per-market files in each market's language with that domain's own translated handles. Priority: .hu (largest translated catalog; the Chatwoot Help Center has a hu locale), then .pl and .bg (Help Center locales exist), then .eu (English). Take the handles from the hreflang alternates on .ro pages rather than crawling .hu, which rate-limits (per the HU audit notes), and include that market's /policies/ URLs, contact channels and the Help Center locale path.
5) .hr (ro-HR) and .it/ro serve Romanian. They could reuse the RO text but must use their own domain URLs. For .it/ro the spec-correct location would be /ro/llms.txt (subpath files cover pages under that path); this is inferred and untested.
6) Re-run a paced link check on every served llms.txt (e.g. monthly, using /collections/{handle}/products.json) because handles get renamed and collections empty out.
